prompt: A JList backed by a DefaultListModel needs add, remove and move-up commands. Complete all three so the model changes correctly and the selection always lands on a valid row.
explanation: A JList never stores the data itself -- every edit goes through the DefaultListModel, and the list repaints because the model fires events. The awkward part is the selection: removing a row can leave the selected index pointing past the end, so the code has to clamp it or clear it when the list empties. Moving an item is a remove followed by an insert one position earlier, and re-selecting the moved index keeps the item under the user's cursor.
hints: songs.getSelectedIndex() returns -1 when nothing is selected -- that is the guard for both removeSelected and moveSelectedUp.
DefaultListModel.remove(index) returns the element it removed, which is exactly what you need to re-insert one row higher.
After removing, compare your saved index with model.getSize() to decide between setSelectedIndex and clearSelection.
